title: One Cell, Many Jobs, Shared Space

scenes.visual: Title card 'One Cell, Many Jobs, Shared Space' on a cream background, 16:9. COLOUR MAP, the same in both films: cell membrane = BLUE outline; cytoplasm = PALE BLUE fluid; nucleus = PURPLE round shape; endoplasmic reticulum (ER) = GREEN folded ribbons; mitochondria = GOLD bean shapes; vacuole and fat drop = PALE CREAM sac. All cells are flat cartoons labelled 'schematic'. Every number appears only as on-screen text.

scenes.tts: Your heart muscle cell and a white fat cell share many of the same kinds of parts. So why do they look nothing alike inside? Let's build a cell and find out.
scenes.visual: Split screen. Left: a long heart muscle cell cartoon packed with GOLD beans around one PURPLE nucleus; a small beating-heart icon above it. Right: a round fat cell almost filled by one PALE CREAM drop, a flat PURPLE nucleus squeezed at the edge. A large question mark pulses between them, then both cells slide off screen.
scenes.narration: Your heart muscle cell and a white fat cell share many of the same kinds of parts. So why do they look nothing alike inside? Let's build a cell and find out.

scenes.tts: Start with the outline. The cell membrane is the thin boundary around the cell. It controls what enters and leaves. Inside is the cytoplasm: a jelly-like fluid and the parts in it, except the nucleus.
scenes.visual: A BLUE outline draws itself as a rounded rectangle in the centre; label 'cell membrane: controls what enters and leaves'. Small arrows try to cross; some pass, some bounce. The outline then fills with PALE BLUE fluid that ripples gently; label 'cytoplasm: fluid plus the parts in it, except the nucleus'.
scenes.narration: Start with the outline. The cell membrane is the thin boundary around the cell. It controls what enters and leaves. Inside is the cytoplasm: a jelly-like fluid and the parts in it, except the nucleus.

scenes.tts: The parts inside are called organelles. An organelle is a small part that does a special job. The nucleus holds the cell's instructions. The E R is a network of folded membranes. It helps make and move many proteins and fats.
scenes.caption: The parts inside are called organelles. An organelle is a small part that does a special job. The nucleus holds the cell's instructions. The ER is a network of folded membranes. It helps make and move many proteins and fats.
scenes.visual: Word 'organelle = small part with a special job' appears at top. A PURPLE nucleus drops into the cell; a scroll icon inside it; label 'nucleus: instructions'. GREEN folded ribbons unfold beside it; label 'endoplasmic reticulum (ER): helps make and move many proteins and fats'. Tiny dots sit on the ribbons, labelled 'ribosomes: tiny protein builders on the ER'; they assemble small blocks labelled 'protein', which then slide along the ribbons.
scenes.narration: The parts inside are called organelles. An organelle is a small part that does a special job. The nucleus holds the cell's instructions. The ER is a network of folded membranes. It helps make and move many proteins and fats.

scenes.tts: Mitochondria release energy stored in food, such as sugar and fats. They release it in a form the cell can use. A vacuole is a sac that stores water, food and wastes. Plant cells have one large vacuole. Many animal cells have only small sacs.
scenes.visual: Three GOLD beans drop in; a small cube labelled 'sugar' enters a bean and a spark leaves it; label 'mitochondria: release energy stored in food'. A PALE CREAM sac appears; label 'vacuole: stores water, food and wastes'. A small inset shows a plant cell with one large cream vacuole beside an animal cell with a few small sacs.
scenes.narration: Mitochondria release energy stored in food, such as sugar and fats. They release it in a form the cell can use. A vacuole is a sac that stores water, food and wastes. Plant cells have one large vacuole. Many animal cells have only small sacs.

scenes.tts: Now give the cell one job: replacing a worn-out protein. The nucleus holds the instructions. The E R helps make the new protein and move it. The mitochondria release the energy that building uses. The membrane lets in food and oxygen.
scenes.caption: Now give the cell one job: replacing a worn-out protein. The nucleus holds the instructions. The ER helps make the new protein and move it. The mitochondria release the energy that building uses. The membrane lets in food and oxygen.
scenes.visual: A lit path traces through the cell as each part is named: a glowing line from the PURPLE nucleus to the GREEN ribbons, where the tiny ribosome dots on the ribbons assemble a new 'protein' block, which the ribbons then carry along, while a faded 'worn-out protein' block is carried away. The GOLD beans pulse, sending small sparks to the ribbons. Arrows labelled 'food' and 'oxygen' cross the BLUE membrane into the PALE BLUE fluid; the food is partly broken down in the fluid before small pieces enter the beans, and oxygen drifts to the beans. Numbers 1 to 4 appear beside the four parts in turn.
scenes.narration: Now give the cell one job: replacing a worn-out protein. The nucleus holds the instructions. The ER helps make the new protein and move it. The mitochondria release the energy that building uses. The membrane lets in food and oxygen.

scenes.tts: Four parts, one job. Every life job needs a team like this. Growth, repair and response each need several parts working at once.
scenes.visual: On-screen text '4 parts, 1 job'. Three more job labels appear around the cell, 'growth', 'repair', 'response', each with thin lines running to several parts at once, so the lines criss-cross the cell.
scenes.narration: Four parts, one job. Every life job needs a team like this. Growth, repair and response each need several parts working at once.

scenes.tts: So what if only the mitochondria stop? Does only energy use slow down, or do other jobs slow down too? Pause and decide.
scenes.visual: The GOLD beans flicker. A card reads 'PAUSE AND PREDICT: if only the mitochondria stop, do other jobs slow down too?' with two buttons, 'only energy use' and 'other jobs too'.
scenes.narration: So what if only the mitochondria stop? Does only energy use slow down, or do other jobs slow down too? Pause and decide.

scenes.visual: The predict card holds; a 5-second ring timer empties.

scenes.tts: Other jobs slow down too. The nucleus and the E R are still fine. But building needs energy, so the repair path slows and stalls. Growth and response slow down with it. No part decides anything; each one simply follows chemistry.
scenes.caption: Other jobs slow down too. The nucleus and the ER are still fine. But building needs energy, so the repair path slows and stalls. Growth and response slow down with it. No part decides anything; each one simply follows chemistry.
scenes.visual: The GOLD beans dim to grey. The sparks fade; the 'protein' block slows and halts halfway along the GREEN ribbons. Three small bars labelled 'growth', 'repair' and 'response' sink partway down one after another, none to zero, while the PURPLE nucleus and GREEN ribbons stay coloured. Text: 'other jobs slow too'.
scenes.narration: Other jobs slow down too. The nucleus and the ER are still fine. But building needs energy, so the repair path slows and stalls. Growth and response slow down with it. No part decides anything; each one simply follows chemistry.

scenes.tts: Here is the second idea. Picture the cell from above, as a floor plan. Each part is a room. Together, the rooms make up the whole cell.
scenes.visual: The mitochondria brighten again. The cell's outline squares off into a floor plan seen from above, labelled 'floor plan = shares of the cell'. Each part becomes a coloured room: PURPLE, GREEN, GOLD, CREAM, with PALE BLUE hallways. A small pie-style tally in the corner shows the room shares adding to 100%.
scenes.narration: Here is the second idea. Picture the cell from above, as a floor plan. Each part is a room. Together, the rooms make up the whole cell.

scenes.tts: So when one room takes a big share, the others take smaller shares. Cells with different jobs often hold their parts in different amounts.
scenes.visual: The same floor plan redraws twice with different room sizes, each time with the corner tally still adding to 100%; no walls push or press. A small note: 'a picture of shares; real cells also grow and shrink'. Text: 'cells with different jobs: often different amounts of each part'.
scenes.narration: So when one room takes a big share, the others take smaller shares. Cells with different jobs often hold their parts in different amounts.

scenes.tts: A heart muscle cell works without a break. It releases a lot of energy, mostly from fats. So mitochondria fill a large share of its space.
scenes.visual: The floor plan relabels 'heart muscle cell'. A beating-heart icon pulses in the corner. The GOLD room grows to about a third of the floor; much of the rest becomes a striped region labelled 'muscle fibres that contract', with a small PURPLE room and thin GREEN strips. Label 'job: work without a break'.
scenes.narration: A heart muscle cell works without a break. It releases a lot of energy, mostly from fats. So mitochondria fill a large share of its space.

scenes.tts: A white fat cell stores fat. So one big fat drop fills most of its space. The other parts sit in a thin rim around the edge.
scenes.visual: A second floor plan slides in beside the first, labelled 'white fat cell' and 'drawn the same size, not to real scale'. One PALE CREAM room expands until it fills most of the floor; the PURPLE, GREEN and a few GOLD rooms squeeze into a thin strip along the walls. Label 'job: store fat'.
scenes.narration: A white fat cell stores fat. So one big fat drop fills most of its space. The other parts sit in a thin rim around the edge.

scenes.tts: Many of the same parts, very different floor plans. A part's size alone does not tell you a cell's job. But comparing parts with jobs can show a pattern.
scenes.visual: The two floor plans fold back into the heart cell and fat cell cartoons from the opening, side by side, matching the opening split screen. Arrows from a 'job' label point to the GOLD region in the heart cell and the CREAM drop in the fat cell. Small text: 'a pattern, not a rule for every cell'.
scenes.narration: Many of the same parts, very different floor plans. A part's size alone does not tell you a cell's job. But comparing parts with jobs can show a pattern.

scenes.visual: End card with the Hex mascot holding a small floor plan. Line: 'Parts work as a team; cells with different jobs hold different amounts.'
